description: The Global Health Access and Outreach Initiative at the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine is a medical student-led organization dedicated to promoting awareness of health disparities that affect populations both internationally and within the United States. description: SAIS GWL is a student organization dedicated to building a community of women leaders at SAIS and to raising awareness around the issues and challenges facing women around the world.

description: We are the Gospel Choir at Johns Hopkins University! Since 1991, we have been spreading the gospel of Jesus Christ to the Hopkins campus and Baltimore community through song, dance, and worship. We aim to provide a setting where people of all backgrounds and races can grow in the love and knowledge of Jesus Christ.

description: The goal of GRACE is to foster networking and support between the graduate women of ECE and CS. Many women in GRACE are the only woman in their lab group, so GRACE provides a space for women in ECE and CS to meet, network, and support each through their times in these departments. This is primarily accomplished by a biweekly bring your own lunches, professional development trainings, networking and mentoring opportunities, and social events.

name: Graduate Christian Fellowship
description: The Graduate Christian Fellowship is affiliated with InterVarsity Christian Fellowship/USA Graduate and Faculty Ministries. We exist to help members of the JHU graduate and post-graduate communities grow in love for God, God's Word, God's people of every ethnicity and culture, and God's purposes in the world.

name: Graduate Healthcare Business Association
description: To be recognized as the leading student association in the realm of Healthcare Business. Our mission is to foster the growth of insightful healthcare leaders equipped with the knowledge and skills required to shape the future of the healthcare industry.

name: Graduate Muslim Students Association
description: We promote interaction and communication among members of the Johns Hopkins community by organizing events and initiatives that increase understanding, education, and appreciation of Islam, and faith in general. We are dedicated to the messages of peace, tolerance, environmental stewardship, community service, health, and human rights. We welcome participation from all interested individuals, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, religion, sexual orientation, disability, or any other identity.

name: Graduate Pickup Soccer
description: Our Pickup Soccer group provides an inclusive and welcoming community where Hopkins affiliates of all backgrounds and demographics can experience the social and health benefits of the world's most popular sport. This mission is achieved through organizing casual, open-access, low-stakes soccer games. Any Johns Hopkins University affiliates—undergraduate and graduate students, faculty, and staff—are welcome to attend our scheduled games. If interested, be sure to become a group member to be notified of games!

name: Graduate Representative Organization
description: To promote graduate student interests, both academic and social, within the University environment and in order to represent graduate students before the faculty and administration of Johns Hopkins University.

The GSC is focused on bringing psychology students together through events like colloquium, community outreach and holiday gatherings. Additionally, we hope to form a community of like-minded students who help and support each other through events like Brain Awareness Week so as to allow students to access all the resources the campus has to offer.

description: GreenHacks seeks to offer a platform for competitive ideation and creativity to spark innovative and sustainable solution design. Through the hackathon format, we bring together forward-looking students, JHU faculty members, sustainability organizations, and companies into one space for the purposes of interaction and collaboration in order to: - Accelerate the conversation regarding innovative sustainable solutions. - Connect people at the intersection of different fields including design, software development, business, engineering, science, and policy. - Encourage creative-thinking, collabo

Each finished work serves as a fruit of our combined efforts, and a stepping stone for future, even greater works. description: HISA aims to unite Johns Hopkins affiliates who have expressed interest in Hawaiian culture and or have ties to the Hawaiian Islands. The organization plans to contribute to the multicultural student body through means of sharing different Hawaiian traditions for all of Johns Hopkins to partake in. Furthermore, HISA aims to provide awareness of culturally relevant events and dilemmas through the form of educational platforms and summits.

description: The purpose of The Health Policy Collective is to bring students together to engage in advocacy and health policy through various avenues. Our group serves as the Hopkins chapter of the AMA, MedChi, and general health policy. The organization seeks to educate students on how policy is created and how we can become involved in advocacy across diverse areas of health policy such as medical education, vaccine mandates, and Medicaid payment structures, to name a few. name: Health Promotion and Well-Being
description: Health Promotion and Well-Being cultivates and supports holistic well-being for individuals, relationships, groups, and the Hopkins community across all schools and divisions.

name: Healthcare not Bombs
description: Healthcare Not Bombs is a student-led organization dedicated to advancing health justice, solidarity, and human rights by opposing militarism and systemic violence, supporting affected communities through mutual aid and advocacy, and educating future health professionals to care for people, not power. We are open to all eligible students without regard to sex, gender, marital status, pregnancy, race, color, ethnicity, national origin, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status or other legally protected characteristic.

name: Healthcare Organizational Leadership Student Network
description: A student network to provide and sustain an inviting space for existing students to develop a network, promote professional and personal growth, excellence in nursing, and student mentorship.

name: Hearts for the Homeless
description: Contribute to the health and well-being of one of the most vulnerable populations in our nation with free heart health screenings, education, and provide clinical outreach opportunities for students who wish to contribute to our effort.

description: As Hermanas of Hermandad de Sigma Iota Alpha Inc., our mission is to uphold the goals set forth by our thirteen founding mothers. We pledge to formalize, cultivate, and foster bonds amongst each other as sisters and abide by respect, trust, communication, professionalism, and accountability.

description: HSC provides a forum for JHU students to learn more about the ideals and practices of Hinduism, through weekly prayer, holiday celebrations, and community outreach. HSC not only aims to foster peace, harmony, and spiritual progress through Hinduism, but also embraces all religions as paths towards universal spirituality.

The Hippocrates Med Review is a medical journal that aims to humanize medicine to make it accessible to those who need the information the most: the patient. Additionally, in recent years, the term "medicine" has been broadened to encompass more than just physical health; mental and economic health, through the lens of medicine, are increasingly important to a patient's quality of life. name: Hippocratic Society Student Chapter
description: Forming and sustaining clinicians in the practice and pursuit of good medicine.

name: History
description: The Department of History offers students the opportunity to work intensively in the classroom and with individual faculty to discover the richness and complexity of history. The department emphasizes the histories of Europe, the United States, Africa, Latin America, and China.

name: History of Art
description: The┬áDepartment of the History of Art┬áoffers unique opportunities for the study of art history thanks to the university's proximity to remarkable collections in Baltimore and Washington, D.C.

name: History of Medicine Interest Group
description: The History of Medicine Interest Group (HMIG) seeks to cultivate an interdisciplinary community of graduate students, faculty, and researchers dedicated to the study and discussion of the historical dimensions of medicine, healthcare, and the healing arts. The group aims to foster intellectual exchange, support ongoing research, and broaden perspectives on how historical contexts shape modern medical practices.

name: History of Science, Medicine & Technology
description: The┬áDepartment of the History of Science and Technology┬áconcentrates on science and technology since the Renaissance. It offers programs in collaboration with the Department of the History of Medicine at the School of Medicine.

description: Hopkins Homeless Outreach and Medical Education (HOME) is a student-led service organization dedicated to serving and advocating for individuals experiencing homelessness in the Baltimore community through direct outreach, medical education, and compassionate care. description: Homewood United for Music is a year-long musical programming committee that serves to support the community of student musicians at JHU. Programming Committee members are students who love music and who have a passion for planning musical performance events.

description: It is our mission as Hop Help Tutoring to provide academic support and act as exemplary role models to the students of Waverly Elementary School so that they are inspired to pursue learning. We tutor students from third to fifth grade three times a week during their after-school program with math and reading homework, while encouraging them to have fun. name: Hop in Motion
description: To inspire and empower individuals with physical disabilities / cognitive impairment in the Baltimore community.

description: Hop-In is a five-week summer program that invites a cohort of incoming first-generation and limited-income/Pell-eligible (FLI) students to build community and experience academic and social life at Johns Hopkins before the beginning of their fall semester. This program offers enrichment opportunities for students to develop professionally and personally as leaders at Johns Hopkins. All incoming participants have access to an upper-class peer mentor, exposure to various academic support resources, and opportunities to interact with faculty.

Organizer applications open in October of each year!!

description: The Hopkins Basic and Translational Research Society (HBTRS) is a student-led organization dedicated to building a community of medical students engaged in basic and translational science. Our goal is to foster collaboration, mentorship, and idea generation by connecting students with peers and physician-scientist faculty across disciplines. name: Hopkins Biotech Network
description: The Hopkins Biotech Network (HBN) is a non-profit student group whose mission is to expose, educate and connect Johns Hopkins students, alumni, postdoctoral fellows, and greater community with opportunities in non-academic careers. We welcome participation from all interested JHSOM students, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, religion, sexual orientation, disability, or any other identity.

name: Hopkins Community Connection
description: Hopkins Community Connection collaborates with communities to challenge systemic barriers to health equity by training a diverse workforce of individuals who champion a more just system through an innovative and patient-centered approach to addressing social determinants of health in the healthcare setting.

name: Hopkins Connect
description: Our aim is simple and clear. Every student will graduate with at least one meaningful mentoring relationship. Our team connects students with mentors via networking programs, flash mentoring, and online opportunities.

name: Hopkins Dance Collective
description: The mission of HDC is to provide a creative and inclusive space for dance and performance that is open to all individuals affiliated with the Johns Hopkins School of Medicine. The organization seeks to foster a community centered on openness, wellness, and connection while encouraging members to explore creativity and self-expression through dance. As a 24/7 rapid response service, HERO provides BLS level care on over 300 calls each year. HERO has approximately 50 active members, each with at least a Maryland EMT-B certification involving 200 hours of classroom learning and over 100 training hours.

name: Hopkins Figure Skating Club
description: The Johns Hopkins Figure Skating club strives to provide skaters an opportunity to skate as a team each week, regardless of their level. Members can pursue their competitive goals as a collegiate skating team, train with coaches at Mount Pleasant Ice Arena, and work with each other to better their abilities as any athletic team strives to do.

name: Hopkins Game Development Society
description: At HGDS, we empower you to create in the world of video games. We run instructional workshops on game development that fill an unmet need in the education landscape at JHU, host networking events with professional game developers, and make games with each other in the club! Our community primarily lives on discord and that is where we do our event annoucements. If you're interested in joining us, paste this invite link into your browser: https://discord.com/invite/AvyRN8Y8wk

name: Hopkins Golf Club
description: Our mission is to bring together medical and graduate students who share a passion for golf. We welcome golfers of all levels, from beginners who are interested in learning to scratch golfers.

name: Hopkins Health Innovation & Technology (HHIT)
description: Hopkins Health Innovation and Technology is a student organization at the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine working across digital health, clinical AI, and health technology. The organization exists to give medical students a way into this work while they are still in training. HHIT connects students with faculty, clinician-innovators, researchers, and companies inside and outside Hopkins. It runs seminars, workshops, speaker events, and coursework on healthcare innovation, and it supports students who want to build and test solutions to problems they encounter in the clinic.

name: Hopkins Hoopers
description: To build a welcoming and inclusive community for medical students of all levels of interest and experience in basketball, fostering camaraderie, fitness, and wellness by providing opportunities to regularly engage in friendly games together.

name: Hopkins Initiative for Keen Explorers and Sightseeing
description: Hopkins HIKES brings students together through safe, accessible, and low-cost outdoor adventures that promote wellness, community, and appreciation for the natural world. We are open to all eligible students without regard to sex, gender, marital status, pregnancy, race, color, ethnicity, national origin, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status or other legally protected characteristic.

name: Hopkins Med Against Gun Violence
description: Hopkins Medicine Against Gun Violence (HMAGV) is a student-led organization dedicated to equipping Johns Hopkins medical students with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to be effective advocates against gun violence. We believe that physicians have both an opportunity and an ethical responsibility to address gun violence as the public health crisis that it is — not only through clinical care, but through direct civic engagement and policy change.

name: Hopkins Med for Harm Reduction
description: Hopkins Med for Harm Reduction educates, volunteers, and advocates to bring harm reduction principles into healthcare and the Baltimore community.

name: Hopkins Med Student Martial Arts Club
Hopkins Med Volo Sports Club
description: The Hopkins Med Volo Sports Club seeks to foster community, wellness, and camaraderie among medical students through recreational and competitive team sports. By organizing and supporting participation in Volo leagues, the club promotes physical activity, stress relief, and teamwork outside of the classroom and hospital, while building connections across classes and disciplines. We welcome participation from all interested JHSOM students, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, religion, sexual orientation, disability, or any other identity.

name: Hopkins Medical Orchestra
description: Relaunched in 2025 after a 13-year hiatus, the Hopkins Medical Orchestra (HMO) is a student-led, non-audition, inclusive community symphonic orchestra producing four free concerts per year, with an artistic direction exploring the intersection of music, medicine, and science. HMO has a growing membership of over 80 musicians encompassing medical practitioners, faculty, staff, students, and community members across the Johns Hopkins East Baltimore campus, along with strong engagement from the wider Hopkins and Baltimore community, with over 500 audience members attending HMO concerts in 2025. name: Hopkins Medicine Cycling
description: The mission of Hopkins Medicine Cycling is to build a community connected by a shared interest in cycling while promoting physical activity, camaraderie, and lifelong participation in the sport. The organization aims to bridge cycling and medicine by exploring the science of performance, training, injury prevention, recovery, and athlete health, with a particular focus on cycling and endurance sports.

name: Hopkins Medicine Gardening
description: Our mission is to promote medical student wellness, environmental stewardship, and community connection through gardening. By cultivating green spaces on the medical campus and collaborating with local partners, we create opportunities for students to connect with nature, practice sustainable gardening, and engage school-aged youth in hands-on environmental education. Together, we aim to nurture healthier communities and a healthier environment.

name: Hopkins Motorsports Club
description: The Hopkins Motorsports Club (HMC) is dedicated to fostering a vibrant community of students, faculty, and staff at the Johns Hopkins School of Medicine who share an interest in motorsports. We welcome participation from all interested JHSOM students, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, religion, sexual orientation, disability, or any other identity.

name: Hopkins Pacemakers
description: Foster community and promote wellness across the School of Medicine through structured runs throughout the Baltimore community.

name: Hopkins Political Union: A Civic Debate and Discussion Society
Hopkins Rugby Football Club (Men's)
description: The Hopkins Rugby Football Club is an organization dedicated to the pursuit of individual and organizational excellence through the unique camaraderie evident in rugby union teams. It is comprised of not only a diverse representation of the schools population both academically and culturally, but also includes student leaders and fraternity presidents. As a year-round organization, the HRFC provides an unmatched and unique experience at Hopkins that can help truly define a four-year undergradute term.

name: Hopkins Semester DC
description: The Hopkins Semester D.C. aims to provide opportunities for all undergraduate students in Washington, D.C. This page serves as a hub for cohort participants, applicants, and interested students to receive information and connect with each other and program leadership.

name: Hopkins Sport Taekwondo Club
description: Hopkins Sport Taekwondo Club (HST) aims to share Taekwondo with the entire campus community, attend tournaments and compete as a team in intercollegiate Taekwondo leagues, and create an inclusive, safe space for every member to learn, find support, set and achieve goals, and grow.

name: Hopkins Student Ballet Company
description: The JHU Ballet Company is a student-run ballet company that enables members to train in the technique and artistry of classical ballet from a healthy perspective that prioritizes enjoyment and well-being. The company holds regular classes open to students of all skill levels. They also choreograph, rehearse, and perform classical and contemporary ballet pieces in inclusive, free-of-charge productions each semester.

name: Hopkins Student Science Fiction and Fantasy Association
description: HopSFA is Johns Hopkins University's very own science fiction and fantasy association. Most of all, HopSFA is about fun. We have biweekly Wednesday meetings with various sci-fi/fantasy-themed events and weekly Saturday board game nights.

name: Hopkins Student Wind Energy Team
description: The Hopkins Student Wind Energy Team (HSWET) aims to expose undergraduate students to the wind energy industry through a combination of hands-on wind turbine design and testing, the creation of a project development plan for a wind farm, and on/off-campus educational initiatives. The team strives to improve the network of renewable energy and sustainable business extracurricular opportunities for undergraduate students at Johns Hopkins and in the broader Baltimore community through their participation in the Department of Energy Collegiate Wind Competition on an annual basis.

name: Hopkins Symphony Orchestra
description: Hopkins Symphony Orchestra provides excellent orchestra concerts and performance opportunities for the JHU and surrounding communities. Hopkins Symphony Orchestra's vision is to be an integral presence in the JHU and surrounding communities as Baltimore City's only community orchestra. Vital to both campus and community life, HSO provides quality performances, educational opportunities, community engagement projects, and collaborations with artistic, social, and educational partners. Except where specified, all goals and strategies apply to both the Symphonic and Concert Orchestras.

name: Hopkins Taekwondo Club
description: Following the original interpretation of Taekwondo (loosely ITF), Hopkins Taekwondo Club seeks to enrich its students through understanding of the mental, physical, and philosophical aspects of this Korean martial art. We focus on both the traditional practice of martial arts, and optional competitions for any of our members to take part it, in both forms and sparring.

name: Hopkins Undergraduate Society for Applied Mathematics
description: HUSAM aims to bring together all Applied Math and Statistics majors on campus through social, educational, and professional events. HUSAM also strives to make all Johns Hopkins students aware of various careers involving AMS and general knowledge about the AMS major on campus. The group also seeks to bring together as many AMS majors and faculty as possible.

name: Hopkins Votes
description: Hopkins Votes is a nonpartisan initiative that provides voter assistance and education to Johns Hopkins University faculty, staff, students, and the wider community. We are committed to facilitating access to the electoral process for all eligible voters, regardless of an individual's political affiliation, location, voting method, or registration status.

name: Hopkins Votes at Peabody

We are committed to facilitating access to the electoral process for all eligible voters, regardless of an individual's political affiliation, location, voting method, or registration status.

name: HopkinsLEAD
description: HopkinsLEAD is for incoming students who want to build a community of authentic leaders while at college. Held the week before Orientation, students will learn how to communicate their own values in order to inspire others and create positive social change at Johns Hopkins and in Baltimore City. HopkinsLEAD is held in collaboration with Orientation and First-Year Experience and is one of eight opportunities to begin building community before classes event start.

name: HopStone Capital
description: Founded in 2022, HopStone Capital is a student-run venture capital organization that serves as a catalyst for Johns Hopkins students to explore entrepreneurship and careers in starutps/VC. Aiming to empower the Johns Hopkins startup ecosystem, HopStone Capital empowers early-stage startups founded by Johns Hopkins affiliates via equity-free grants.

name: HOPSY
description: HOPSY is Johns Hopkins' Medical School Psychiatry Interest Group. Through student and faculty events, we seek to increase the exposure of medical students to the field of psychiatry and connect them with psychiatry resources in the medical school and community. We welcome participation from all interested JHSOM students, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, religion, sexual orientation, disability, or any other identity.

name: HopTEA
description: The mission of the Themed Entertainment Association at Johns Hopkins University (TEA@JHU, HopTEA) is to serve as a multidisciplinary professional organization providing students with practical experience in the themed entertainment industry. By giving students opportunities to tour theme parks, participate in design competitions, learn from industry professionals, and attend conferences, it is our goal to show our members the full extent of this industry and help them meet their career goals.

name: HopTHON at Johns Hopkins University
description: HopTHON at Johns Hopkins University is a student-run movement dedicated to year-round fundraising for our local Children's Miracle Network Hospital, the Johns Hopkins Children's Center. Our mission is to help kids be kids, regardless of age or health status, because everyone deserves the chance to enjoy their life. We're one generation fighting for the next.

name: Humanistic Anatomy Society

We organize an event honoring body donors which is attended by both anatomy students and the families of the donors. We also provide emotional and spiritual support for anatomy students throughout human anatomy and offer spaces for constructive thought around the experience. name: Humans in Health
description: Our group, Humans in Health, seeks to create a journal magazine that highlights and explores the diversity of medical and healing practices, how these practices treat different types of conditions, and how they intersect with Western medicine. The magazine will feature interviews with those who practice forms of health and/or medicine unique to their own culture and/or have experience blending their healing with Western medicine.

In addition, IGSA actively engages with the incoming graduate students with a welcome event and a host of info sessions.

IAMSA strives to empower future leaders in medicine who value diversity, inclusion, and equity in healthcare.

description: A student group dedicated to exploring and celebrating Israeli culture.

name: IT@JH
description: IT@JH supports and enhances research, teaching, and patient care at Johns Hopkins through effective use of excellent information technology resources, products, and services.

description: At Ivy League+ at Johns Hopkins (ILJH) Pre Health Society, our mission is to propel undergraduate students towards becoming future healthcare leaders by fostering unparalleled cross-campus connections across top institutions. name: J-Card Office
description: The J-Card gets you into residence halls, the library, academic buildings, and other campus facilities. It's also as good as cash: You can store money on your J-Card and use it to buy food and other items on and off campus. Make copies, do laundry, buy a pizza: It's accepted by more than a dozen businesses in Charles Village.

name: J.B. Grant Global Health Society
description: The JB Grant Global Health Society is dedicated to fostering a global health community that transcends boundaries, embraces diversity, and takes action to improve the health and well-being of our global community. We aim to empower students with the knowledge, skills, and opportunities necessary to make a meaningful impact on global health issues.

description: The Johns Hopkins Jail Tutorial Program provides tutoring in GED and other subjects to incarcerated men, women, and juveniles at institutions across Baltimore and Maryland. Tutors have the opportunity to build unique relationships with inmates and develop a personalized curriculum for tutees. Many incarcerated in multiple institutions lack educational opportunities to prepare themselves after release, and Jail Tutorial Project aims to bridge this gap. JASA activities include cooking and eating Japanese food, watching Japanese films, going to D.C. for Japanese festivals, and meeting Japanese organizations from other areas.

description: Jaywalk Dance Team, founded in 2007, is a student dance team at Johns Hopkins University. Known for its strong technique and emphasis on dynamic student choreography, Jaywalk primarily performs jazz, contemporary and lyrical, but our members come from diverse training backgrounds. Student-run and student-choreographed, Jaywalk is dedicated to presenting the highest level of performance and technique at JHU.

name: Jewish Business Association
description: The Jewish Business Association is an organization that serves as a resource to connect, inform, and support the Jewish community on campus. description: The mission of JHU’s Jewish Student Nurses’ Association is to provide space for Jewish students to connect and a means for all members of the community to experience Jewish culture and learn about the notion of “tikkun olam,” or “repairing the world,” and how it intersects with our role as nurses. Open to both Jewish and non-Jewish students!

name: Jewish Student Athlete Association
description: Our mission is to bring together Jewish Student Athletes in a culturally familiar environment for Shabbat, to support each other in athletic competition, and to talk about athletic events such as the Maccabiah games.

name: Jewish Student Life at Peabody
description: The Jewish Life at Peabody group is dedicated to offering opportunities for Jewish students at Peabody to explore and practice their Judaism through social, religious, and cultural events.

name: Jewish Students Association
description: Celebrating Jewish life, building community for all.

name: Jewish Students Association at SAIS

name: JHU German Club
description: The Johns Hopkins University (JHU) German Club is the primary vehicle through which members of the Hopkins community can express their appreciation for the German language and culture and interface with similarly-motivated individuals. It is also a platform for everyone to learn and grow on their path of language acquisition and culture appreciation.

name: JHU Makerspace
description: The JHU Makerspace is located at 320 W 29th St #220 (across the street from R House). The Makerspace is a manufacturing and design space managed by the Whiting School of Engineering to enable innovative projects by students. The Makerspace is open to all students, faculty, and staff of Johns Hopkins University. Priority is given to personal projects unrelated to coursework or grant-funded research projects that have not yet reached the point of commercialization.

name: JHU Pet and Animal Welfare Society
description: The JHU Pet and Animal Welfare Society (JHU PAWS) aims to improve the quality of life of homeless animals in the Baltimore community through volunteering at the Maryland SPCA, donating handmade pet toys, and fundraising to provide much-needed care and medical treatment. The club is also committed to fostering student well-being and community connection by organizing stress-relief events with therapy dogs before final exams.

name: Johns Hopkins Barbell Club

description: Brazilian Jiu Jitsu is a grappling and ground-fighting sport with a focus of control and submission of your opponent without punching or striking. Our club exists as a safe place for members to practice their skills and grow their knowledge in the sport. Join us Tuesdays and Thursday 7-10pm in MPR A on the 3rd floor of the Rec Center. The best time for beginners is 7-8pm during the guided instruction from our amazing coaches. Open mat is Saturday 2-5pm and Sunday 10-1pm.

We are one of the first collegiate dragon boat clubs on the East Coast. Dragon boat is an activity that incorporates strong values such as leadership, teamwork, and dedication. As a member of this club, you will have the opportunity to travel to races and festivals up and down the East Coast and meet paddlers from well-established dragon boat teams.

description: The Johns Hopkins Entertainers Club is JHU’s one and only fire spinning club. We practice flow arts, a movement-based art form that combines prop manipulation and dance elements. No experience necessary to join - come check us out to learn why we’re known as the “hottest club on campus!”

The JHUDC supports entry to tournaments, holds team-wide practices, and hosts social events, open to all members of the team.

We aim to be a safe and inclusive space for members to express themselves through dance.

Through our collaborative relationships with academic institutions, medical professionals, and community partners, we build bridges of opportunity for aspiring healthcare leaders from all backgrounds, including under-resourced and/or underserved backgrounds, to successfully navigate the pre-med/pre-health pathways at Johns Hopkins and beyond. KBN serves to foster a community among Johns Hopkins University's students, faculty, and staff regardless of gender, race, or ethnic origins to promote the education and open dialogue of the struggles men and women may face because of their natural hair. Furthermore, KBN will serve to empower all individuals to embrace their natural hair.

description: We, as the Korean Peabody Graduate Students Association at Johns Hopkins University, are composed of Korean graduate students dedicated to fostering musical exchange within our community. Our purpose is to organize annual concerts and events, donating the proceeds to benefit the local community. Through these initiatives, we aim to provide constructive support, opportunities, and entertainment for our members, sharing our musical experiences and expertise while giving back to the regional community.

name: Korean Students Association

name: KPM (Korean Pop Motion)
description: KPM was founded in 2015, and we are the first and only, award-winning K-Pop cover dance group on the Johns Hopkins University campus. KPM seeks to promote an awareness of K-Pop and by doing so, foster artistic talent and expression.

name: KROSS
description: KROSS is an on-campus, Korean-Christian fellowship at Johns Hopkins University. KROSS strives to build a community where God lives in His Spirit and where students are reminded of their callings as Gods servants.

name: Lacrosse, Women's Club

The club seeks to promote athletic excellence, teamwork, and leadership while fostering a supportive community on and off the field.

name: Ladybirds Dance Team
description: The official dance team of Johns Hopkins University, The Ladybirds Dance Team, is a completely student-run and student-choreographed team. Focusing on a variety of dance styles, including pom, lyrical/contemporary, and jazz, members come from diverse dance backgrounds and are encouraged to contribute their styles in choreography throughout the year, culminating in the annual Ladybirds Spring Showcase held in Shriver Hall. We seek highly motivated and inspired students who will one day become the great health professionals of tomorrow. We encourage pre-health students that have the desire to pursue clinical and scientific research to pursue their passions. Additionally, we strive to serve the often overlooked Latino population in Baltimore.

name: Lan Yun Blue Orchids Chinese Dance Team
description: Lan Yun Blue Orchids is a performing arts group for students to come together to learn and practice traditional Chinese dance. Dancers of all levels of experience are welcome! Much like the orchid, a complex flower that is uniquely shaped, the Lan Yun Chinese Dance team seeks to promote the understanding of a rich and intricate culture through unique dance moves.

description: Originally founded in 1958, under the auspices of the JHU Chaplain’s Office, the Johns Hopkins Tutorial Project is an after-school tutoring program housed at the Center for Social Concern that provides academic support for elementary school students (grades 1-5). Children are paired with Johns Hopkins University students and receive one-on-one tutoring in reading and math. For nine to ten weeks each semester, approximately 120 children come to the Homewood campus twice a week for tutoring. The children are transported by either the program’s bus or by their families. name: U.S. Army ROTC
description: The ROTC program is structured with classes in leadership development, military skill, and career training with a lab to apply the lessons learned from class. ROTC is the top program in the country for a military test drive as well as the top producing program of United States Army Leaders.

name: Undergraduate Aspiring Physician Scientists Association
description: The JHU Undergraduate APSA will operate for the purpose of supporting the growth and training of aspiring physician-scientists on the Homewood campus; helping build a nurturing community of aspiring physician-scientists at a local, regional, and national level; and promoting the integration of medicine and research through outreach and education. name: Undergraduate History Association
description: The Undergraduate History Association seeks to increase engagement with the discipline of history among undergraduate students through panels, social events, networking events, and discourse. Furthermore, UHA seeks to increase engagement between the history department itself and the JHU community at large. This organization is open to everyone, including those who are not declared majors/minors.

name: Undergraduate Steering Committee - Psychology Department
description: Our mission is to provide undergraduate students pursuing a degree in psychology with any support and guidance they might need through their time at JHU. The USC is focused on bringing psychology students together through events like Lunches with a Psychology Professor and Research Panels. Additionally, we hope to form a community of like-minded students who help and support each other through events like Crash Course and the Mentorship Program so as to allow students to access all the resources the campus has to offer.

name: Universities Allied for Essential Medicines
description: JHU UAEM's mission is to improve aspects of JHU's Report Card with regards to innovation, access, transparency, empowerment, and COVID-19 by advocating for open source research while promoting and managing R&D at Hopkins for those who are disproportionately affected by the access to medicines crisis. Our work is guided at all times by principles of non-partisanship, democracy, transparency, solidarity, and respect.

name: University Experiential Learning
description: To enrich and enhance the overall learning experience of our students by providing part-time work experiences and paid campus internships that foster leadership development, provides transferable life skills, enables career development, and allows for the integration of classroom learning with the work experience.

name: VentureNest
description: VentureNest at Johns Hopkins University is a student-led incubator dedicated to empowering aspiring entrepreneurs to transform innovative ideas into successful ventures. We provide a collaborative ecosystem that fosters creativity, mentorship, and skill development, enabling students to launch impactful startups, drive change, and create sustainable value in their communities and beyond.

name: Vietnamese Students Association
description: The Johns Hopkins University Vietnamese Students Association (VSA) strives to build community and advocate for Vietnamese students at Johns Hopkins University. We aim to achieve this by developing social, cultural, and educational events that increase awareness of the Vietnamese heritage and lived experience, while promoting solidarity with other marginalized student communities.

name: Viola De Gamba
description: The Viola Da Gamba Club creates a welcoming space for students to play or hear the Viol and its unique sound, collaborate and play as a group, and share early and modern Viola Da Gamba music with the conservatory community.

name: Violet at Hopkins

name: ViSION (Vision Screening In Our Neighborhoods)
description: Vision Screening in Our Neighborhoods (ViSION) is dedicated to bridging gaps in eyecare in and around Baltimore City. We partner with organizations that have existing community relationships to conduct comprehensive vision screenings with a particular focus on identifying early signs of glaucoma, which, if left untreated, can lead to blindness. name: Volunteers for Medical Engineering
description: The Johns Hopkins Volunteers for Medical Engineering (JHU-VME) is a branch chapter of The IMAGE Center of Maryland, a non-profit organization dedicated to improving the lives of individuals with disabilities in the greater Baltimore community. Our mission centers around three pillars: developing innovative assistive devices, providing service to the local community, and fostering teamwork among our members. name: Voyage Newsletter Club
description: We aim to create an inclusive space where students can explore, appreciate, and share the beauty of nature. Unlike other outdoor clubs at Johns Hopkins, our focus lies in active reflection driven by content creation and media publication. We organize one to two outdoor events each month, during which students document their experiences through journals, vlogs, or other creative narrative methods. Following each event, members submit their stories and vote on the most compelling entry to be featured on the club’s newsletter website. name: Wargaming Club at SAIS
description: The purpose of WGC shall be to enhance students’ understanding of strategy, defense, planning and history through the medium of wargaming.

name: Wing Chun at Johns Hopkins University
description: Wing Chun at Johns Hopkins University (also known as Wing Chun @ JHU, hereinafter referred to as WC@JHU) is a Johns Hopkins University student organization that is dedicated to the teaching of members of the JHU community self-defense through the Wing Chun Kung Fu (hereinafter referred to as Wing Chun) system. To this end, WC@JHU will hold several weekly practices on and off campus taught by the instructors. WC@JHU will also be secondarily dedicated to spreading awareness and interest for kung fu as a whole. To this end, the club will hold outreach events promoting kung fu and martial arts.

name: Witness Theater
description: The purpose of Witness Theater is to provide a platform by which student writers, actors, directors and theater technicians can practice their craft, and to showcase works of theater written by members of the Johns Hopkins University community.

name: WJHU Johns Hopkins Student Radio
description: WJHU Radio, also known as Johns Hopkins Student Radio, is the student-run, internet-based radio station of The Johns Hopkins University. WJHU Radio aims to foster self-expression, creativity, and a sense of community by providing a versatile platform for JHU affiliates to broadcast freeform radio shows and share media of both creative and journalistic nature. Our purpose is to encourage our members and listeners alike to share and explore new perspectives via engagement with the arts as well as offer a support system to students and staff by means of creative outlet and community guidance.

name: Women in Business at Johns Hopkins University
description: Women in Business at JHU - or WiB - was founded to empower undergraduate women to become leaders in the business field. We hope to create a network in the Hopkins community that will help young women develop professionally and achieve their career goals. We plan on achieving this through student and alumni panels on different business fields, resume and interview workshops, mentorship programs, a speaker series, and networking events.

name: Women in Computer Science
description: Women in CS (WiCS) is for women/non-binary individuals, as well as other underrepresented groups in tech (and allies!), who are involved in CS (whether it's majoring, minoring, or seriously considering majoring/minoring). We focus on: - forming friendships - helping you find internships and jobs - providing a welcoming place to both work and hang out

name: Women in Cybersecurity JHU
description: We are the Women in Cybersecurity (WiCyS) Student Chapter at Johns Hopkins University. The goal of this group is to foster and promote sharing of industry knowledge, networking, mentoring, and recruitment with an emphasis on gender equality in the field of cybersecurity. We seek to build a community of growth and support for women and male allies interested in security-related challenges and learning more about the latest security advances. name: Women in Orthopaedics
description: Our mission is to empower women in orthopaedics to thrive, lead, and shape the future of the field. Through mentorship, community, education, and advocacy, we strive to build a culture where women are supported at every stage of their careers and where diverse perspectives strengthen the practice of orthopaedics.

name: Women of Whiting
description: Women of Whiting is a graduate student organization that supports women in STEM through professional development, social, and outreach events. Our members are primarily from the Whiting School of Engineering, Krieger School of Arts and Sciences, and the School of Medicine. The organization is designed to serve masters students, predoctoral students, and postdoctoral fellows. Our aim is to build an inclusive and supportive community for women in STEM and to help students prepare for facing the challenges of graduate school and professional life. name: Women's Club Basketball
description: We are JHU's Womens Club Basketball team! We practice twice a week and play in the National Club Basketball Association (NCBBA) league throughout the year. We're always welcome to having people of all levels, so please reach out! Email: jhuclubbball@gmail.com

name: Women's Club Soccer
description: Did you play Varsity soccer in high school but just don't have the time to make the commitment to the D3 team here?┬á Come try out for Women's Club Soccer!┬á We are a self-motivated team, competing against other club teams in the Baltimore/Delaware region. We are also a tight knit group of friends who have a good time! Feel free visit us during the Student Involvement Fair or to email jhusoccer@gmail.com for more information and to get added to our mailing list.

name: Women's Club Volleyball at Johns Hopkins University
description: The JHU Women's Club Volleyball team (which will be referred to as "team" or "club volleyball") is an organization on campus that provides the opportunity for Johns Hopkins students with previous volleyball experience to participate in regular volleyball play.

Our society consists of female-identifying undergraduate students who have demonstrated academic excellence, commitment to community service, and a passion in pre-health studies. name: Workshop - A Visual Arts Collective
description: The mission of this organization is to provide a space for students to explore their creativity outside of their typical creative disciplines, and to improve student mental health through opportunities to self-express, process emotions, and connect with peers. We intend to build a community at Peabody where students can express their values, feelings, and causes through their work.

description: The mission of the Engineering Advising Office within WSE Undergraduate Academic Affairs is to support the WSE mission to prepare undergraduates to be 21st century leaders by providing an outstanding engineering education and enabling undergraduates to participate fully in the research and translational activities of the school. To accomplish this we: Advise, support, and educate students so that they are able to achieve intellectual, personal, and professional growth. name: YO! Baltimore Tutoring Project
description: The mission of the YO! Baltimore Tutoring Project is to help Baltimore City youth obtain the proper education needed to succeed in life. YO! serves out-of-school youth (16-22 years of age) by tutoring and helping them with academic classes, GED prep and job training. The YO! Center is a short, 5-minute, walk from the Johns Hopkins Medical Campus.
